objects.description: Enumeration of the tag file sort order. Values indicate unsorted, case-sensitive sorted, and case-folded sorted respectively. Macro sortType is an alias unless TAG_NO_COMPAT_SORT_TYPE is defined.
Boolean-like result code used by API functions to indicate success or failure.
Enumeration of library-defined error codes returned by tagsGetErrno() for API-level errors (negative values).

struct sTagFile;

typedef struct sTagFile tagFile;
objects.description: Opaque handle type representing an open tags file context. Only an incomplete declaration is provided here; the structure layout is private to the implementation.
Holds metadata about a tags file and the generating program, plus open status and error information. Populated by tagsOpen().
Represents a single key/value extension field from a tag entry’s extensions section.
Describes one tag entry retrieved from a tags file, including its name, source file, location (pattern or line), kind, file-scope flag, and a list of extension fields.

functions.name: tagsOpen
functions.signature: extern tagFile *tagsOpen (const char *const filePath, tagFileInfo *const info);
functions.description: Opens a tags file for reading and optionally fills tagFileInfo with metadata about the file and creator. Returns an opaque tagFile handle on success or NULL on failure. On success, info->status.opened is set to true; on failure, info->status.opened is false and info->status.error_number contains either an errno value or a tagErrno describing the failure (ENOMEM if handle allocation failed). Intended to be called before all other API functions.
requirements: Must be called before any other function in this API that operates on a tag file.
filePath must point to a valid path to a tags file readable by the process.
info may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagFileInfo and will be populated.
On failure, callers should check info->status.error_number for errno or tagErrno details if info is non-NULL.
The returned tagFile* must be passed to tagsClose() when finished.

functions.name: tagsSetSortType
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsSetSortType (tagFile *const file, const tagSortType type);
functions.description: Overrides automatic detection of the tags file sorting method. Permissible values are TAG_UNSORTED, TAG_SORTED, or TAG_FOLDSORTED. Helps enable fast binary lookups when the original-format tags file lacks sort metadata; incorrect overrides can cause incorrect lookup results.
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle obtained from tagsOpen().
type must be one of TAG_UNSORTED, TAG_SORTED, or TAG_FOLDSORTED.
Returns TagSuccess if called on an open tag file; TagFailure otherwise.
Marking a file as sorted when it is not may lead to incorrect lookup results.

functions.name: tagsFirst
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsFirst (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry);
functions.description: Reads the first tag entry from the opened tags file. If entry is non-NULL, it is populated with the tag’s data. Returns TagSuccess if a tag exists, TagFailure if none (e.g., end of file).
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
Returns TagFailure when no tag is found (end of file).

functions.name: tagsNext
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsNext (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry);
functions.description: Advances to and reads the next tag entry in the file. If entry is non-NULL, it is populated with the tag’s data. Returns TagSuccess if another tag is found, TagFailure on end of file. The first tag is available immediately after tagsOpen().
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
Returns TagFailure when no more tags are available (end of file).

functions.name: tagsField
functions.signature: extern const char *tagsField (const tagEntry *const entry, const char *const key);
functions.description: Retrieves the value of an extension field for a given key from a previously populated tagEntry. Returns a pointer to the value string if present, or NULL if the key is not found. The value may be an empty string.
requirements: entry must have been populated by a prior call to tagsNext(), tagsFind(), or tagsFindNext().
key must point to the desired extension field key string (non-NULL).
The returned pointer is valid as long as the underlying entry data remains valid (lifetime unspecified beyond the scope of the library’s iteration/lookup).

functions.name: tagsFind
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsFind (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry, const char *const name, const int options);
functions.description: Finds the first tag whose name matches the supplied name under the specified options and, if entry is non-NULL, populates it. Uses a fast binary search when the file is sorted (C locale) and case-sensitive matching is requested. Options are a bitwise OR of TAG_FULLMATCH or TAG_PARTIALMATCH and TAG_OBSERVECASE or TAG_IGNORECASE.
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
name must point to the search string (non-NULL).
options must combine one of TAG_FULLMATCH or TAG_PARTIALMATCH with one of TAG_OBSERVECASE or TAG_IGNORECASE.
Binary search is enabled only when the file is sorted using the C locale and TAG_OBSERVECASE is used; TAG_IGNORECASE disables binary search.
Returns TagSuccess if a matching tag is found; TagFailure otherwise.

functions.name: tagsFindNext
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsFindNext (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry);
functions.description: Finds the next tag matching the same name and options used in the most recent tagsFind() call on the same tagFile. If entry is non-NULL, it is populated with the next match. Returns TagSuccess if another match is found, TagFailure otherwise.
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
Must be preceded by a successful call to tagsFind() on the same tagFile to establish the search context.
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
Returns TagFailure if no further matches exist.

functions.name: tagsFirstPseudoTag
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsFirstPseudoTag (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry);
functions.description: Reads the first pseudo tag entry from the opened tags file. If entry is non-NULL, it is populated. Intended for iterating pseudo tags when not directly accessible via tagFileInfo.
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
Returns TagSuccess if a pseudo tag is available; TagFailure on end of pseudo tags or if none exist.

functions.name: tagsNextPseudoTag
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsNextPseudoTag (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry);
functions.description: Advances to and reads the next pseudo tag entry. Use together with tagsFirstPseudoTag(). Returns TagSuccess if another pseudo tag is found, TagFailure otherwise.
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
Should be called after tagsFirstPseudoTag() to iterate pseudo tags.
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
Returns TagFailure when no further pseudo tags are available.

functions.name: tagsFindPseudoTag
functions.signature: extern tagResult tagsFindPseudoTag (tagFile *const file, tagEntry *const entry, const char *const name, const int match);
functions.description: Finds the first pseudo tag whose name matches the supplied name under the specified match mode and, if entry is non-NULL, populates it. Unlike tagsFind(), this uses linear search even if the tags file is sorted. Match is TAG_FULLMATCH or TAG_PARTIALMATCH.
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
entry may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage for tagEntry.
name must point to the search string (non-NULL).
match must be either TAG_FULLMATCH or TAG_PARTIALMATCH.
Returns TagSuccess if a matching pseudo tag is found; TagFailure otherwise.

functions.name: tagsClose
functions.description: Closes the tags file and frees internal resources. Returns TagSuccess if a file was open; TagFailure if no file is currently open.
requirements: file must be a tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen(); may be NULL or invalid, in which case the function returns TagFailure.
After successful return, the handle must not be used in subsequent API calls.

functions.name: tagsGetErrno
functions.description: Returns the error status from the last API call to distinguish between "not found" and actual errors. Returns 0 when an operation failed due to no matching tag; otherwise returns an errno or tagErrno describing the error. Does not report results for tagsOpen(), tagsClose(), or tagsField().
requirements: file must be a valid, open tagFile handle returned by tagsOpen().
Meaningful only for API calls other than tagsOpen(), tagsClose(), and tagsField().
A return of 0 indicates a "not found" condition; nonzero indicates a system errno or tagErrno for an error.

data_types.description: Arbitrary byte string data interpreted as a C-style UTF-8/byte sequence with no specific required format. May be empty and can contain any bytes. Used where APIs accept an unconstrained key or name string.

A file in Exuberant Ctags/Universal Ctags format. Typically a text file with an optional header of pseudo-tags (lines starting with !_TAG_), followed by lines of the form: <tagName><TAB><filePath><TAB><exCmd>;"<TAB><extensionFields>. Sorting and format version may vary. The API reads and parses this file to iterate and search tag entries.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets a "generic string" input used by fuzzer stubs for:
# - tagsFind: name string (non-NULL), options provided separately by fuzzer
# - tagsFindPseudoTag: name string (non-NULL)
# - tagsField: key string (non-NULL)
#
# Goal: Provide valid, interesting strings that are likely to exist in typical
# ctags-style tag files and exercise different behaviors:
# - Common identifiers (main, init, printf, Class, _start)
# - Pseudo tags like "_TAG_FILE_FORMAT", "_TAG_FILE_SORTED", "_TAG_PROGRAM_NAME",
#   "_TAG_PROGRAM_AUTHOR", "_TAG_PROGRAM_URL", "_TAG_PROGRAM_VERSION"
# - Case variants to trigger case-sensitive/insensitive paths
# - Partial-match friendly substrings
# - Extension field keys commonly used in extended format: "kind", "line",
#   "pattern", "file", "language", "scope", "class", "struct", "enum",
#   "namespace", "signature", "arity"
# - Edge cases: empty string, single char, very long identifier, unicode, bytes
# - Regex-like patterns often found in tag patterns (delimiters, escapes)
#
# The fuzzer infra consumes a single bytes buffer and splits it for FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# calls. We thus serialize a small corpus separated by NULs so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# can pick one slice. The content is valid UTF-8/byte strings; empty segment is
# represented by a NULNUL sequence.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[bytes], weights: List[int]) -> bytes:
    total = sum(weights)
    pick = rng.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if pick < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=48) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    s = first + "".join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(n - 1))
    return s.encode('utf-8')

def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a short unicodey string mixing ascii and some BMP code points
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)):
        choice = rng.randrange(4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters))
        elif choice == 1:
            parts.append(chr(rng.randint(0x00A0, 0x024F)))  # Latin-1 Supplement/Extended-B
        elif choice == 2:
            parts.append(chr(rng.randint(0x0370, 0x03FF)))  # Greek
        else:
            parts.append(chr(rng.randint(0x0400, 0x04FF)))  # Cyrillic
    return "".join(parts).encode('utf-8')

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=64) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def _build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []

    # Pseudo tag names (for tagsFindPseudoTag)
    pseudo = [
        b"_TAG_FILE_FORMAT",
        b"_TAG_FILE_SORTED",
        b"_TAG_PROGRAM_NAME",
        b"_TAG_PROGRAM_AUTHOR",
        b"_TAG_PROGRAM_URL",
        b"_TAG_PROGRAM_VERSION",
    ]
    corpus.extend(pseudo)

    # Common identifiers likely to appear in tags
    idents = [
        b"main", b"init", b"printf", b"scanf", b"_start", b"WinMain",
        b"Class", b"constructor", b"destructor", b"operator==", b"foo", b"bar",
        b"Baz", b"qux", b"update", b"render", b"Add", b"remove", b"push_back",
        b"emplace", b"size", b"begin", b"end", b"lambda", b"Lambda",
    ]
    corpus.extend(idents)

    # Case variants to exercise TAG_OBSERVECASE vs TAG_IGNORECASE
    corpus.extend([b"Main", b"MAIN", b"printf", b"PRINTF", b"PrintF"])

    # Extension field keys (for tagsField)
    ext_keys = [
        b"kind", b"line", b"pattern", b"file", b"language", b"scope",
        b"class", b"struct", b"enum", b"namespace", b"signature", b"arity",
        b"typeref", b"inherits", b"implementation",
    ]
    corpus.extend(ext_keys)

    # Patterns and regex-like content typical in tag pattern fields
    patterns = [
        rb"/^int\s+main\s*\(.*\)\s*{/;\"",
        rb"/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\(/;\"",
        rb"/class\s+\w+\s*{/;\"",
        rb"/def\s+\w+\(/;\"",
        rb"/^#define\s+\w+/;\"",
    ]
    corpus.extend(patterns)

    # Edge cases: empty and 1-char
    corpus.append(b"")
    corpus.extend([b"a", b"_", b"$", b" "])

    # Long identifier
    long_ident = b"VeryLongIdentifier_" + b"X" * 120
    corpus.append(long_ident)

    # Unicode examples
    for _ in range(5):
        corpus.append(_rand_unicode(rng))

    # Random identifiers
    for _ in range(10):
        corpus.append(_rand_ident(rng))

    # Random raw bytes segments (valid for generic string)
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(_rand_bytes(rng, 0, 48))

    # Substrings good for partial matches
    corpus.extend([b"prin", b"main", b"_TAG", b"class", b"name", b"url", b"ver"]) 

    # Namespaces and scopes
    corpus.extend([b"ns::Class", b"std::vector", b"MyNS::Inner::Thing"]) 

    # Function signatures or templated names
    corpus.extend([b"func<int>", b"operator<", b"operator>", b"operator[]", b"~Destructor"]) 

    return corpus


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    corpus = _build_corpus(rng)

    # Build an output buffer by selecting a random subset and joining with NULs
    # so the fuzzer can split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations.
    # Ensure total size <= MAX_TOTAL.
    rng.shuffle(corpus)

    out = bytearray()
    # Decide how many segments to include; aim for 8-32
    target_segments = rng.randint(8, 24)

    i = 0
    while i < len(corpus) and target_segments > 0 and len(out) < MAX_TOTAL:
        seg = corpus[i]
        i += 1
        # Occasionally force empty string segments to test empty names/keys
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            seg = b""
        # Occasionally produce case-varied version of an identifier-like segment
        if seg and seg.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.3:
            pick = rng.randrange(3)
            if pick == 0:
                seg = seg.lower()
            elif pick == 1:
                seg = seg.upper()
            else:
                # Title case
                try:
                    seg = seg.decode('utf-8').title().encode('utf-8')
                except UnicodeDecodeError:
                    pass
        # Append with NUL separator
        needed = len(seg) + (1 if out else 0)
        if len(out) + needed > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        if out:
            out.append(0)
        out.extend(seg)
        target_segments -= 1

    # Guarantee at least one segment; if empty, add an empty and a common key
    if not out:
        out.extend(b"\x00kind")

    return bytes(out)

import random
import io
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Universal/Exuberant ctags tags file generator
# We aim to create valid, parseable tag files that exercise:
# - Header pseudo-tags with various sort settings and formats
# - Sorted and unsorted bodies
# - Lines using exCmd as search patterns and as line numbers
# - Extension fields including kind, file scope, language, etc.
# - Mixed case names to exercise observe/ignore case search
# - Multiple entries with the same name to enable Find/FindNext
# - Reasonable path values
# Output limited to <= 4096 bytes

MAX_BYTES = 4096

# Pseudo-tag templates: name, value
PSEUDO_TAGS = [
    ("!_TAG_FILE_FORMAT", "2\t/extended format/"),
    ("!_TAG_FILE_SORTED", "1\t/0=unsorted, 1=sorted, 2=foldcase/"),
    ("!_TAG_PROGRAM_AUTHOR", "Jane Doe\t/jdoe@example.com/"),
    ("!_TAG_PROGRAM_NAME", "utagsgen"),
    ("!_TAG_PROGRAM_URL", "https://example.invalid/ctags"),
    ("!_TAG_PROGRAM_VERSION", "1.2.3"),
]

KINDS = [
    ("f", "function"),
    ("v", "variable"),
    ("c", "class"),
    ("s", "struct"),
    ("m", "macro"),
    ("t", "typedef"),
]

LANGS = ["C", "C++", "Python", "Go", "Rust", "Java", "JavaScript"]

FILES = [
    "src/main.c",
    "src/util.c",
    "include/util.h",
    "lib/module.cpp",
    "pkg/mod.rs",
    "app.py",
    "src/main.go",
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha", "bravo", "charlie", "delta", "echo", "Foobar", "foobar",
    "Gamma", "gamma", "Process", "process", "Update", "update",
    "FindMe", "findme", "Node", "node", "compute", "Compute",
]

ESCAPE_CHARS = "/^$.*+?{}[]()|\\"  # characters we might include in patterns


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(0, len(seq))]


def make_pattern_excmd(rng: random.Random, tagname: str) -> str:
    # Create a search pattern ex command like /^...$/
    # Ensure it contains the tagname for realistic matching; escape slashes
    base = tagname
    # Sprinkle some regexish characters safely
    extras = ''.join(rng.choice(ESCAPE_CHARS) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)))
    content = (base + extras).replace("/", r"\/")
    return f"/^\t{content}\t$/"  # put tabs inside to test robust parsing, escaped by /\t


def make_line_excmd(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Return a positive line number as string
    return str(rng.randint(1, 100000))


def make_ext_fields(rng: random.Random, kind_letter: str, duplicate_name_group: str) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    fields = []
    # kind field by name and/or letter
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        fields.append(("kind", kind_letter))
    # file scope flag
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        fields.append(("file", "1" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "0"))
    # language
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        fields.append(("language", rand_choice(rng, LANGS)))
    # custom fields
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        fields.append(("signature", f"({rng.choice(['int','void','char*','size_t'])})"))
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and duplicate_name_group:
        fields.append(("group", duplicate_name_group))
    # empty value field case
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        fields.append(("note", ""))
    return fields


def assemble_ext_fields(fields: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
    if not fields:
        return ""
    parts = []
    for k, v in fields:
        # Each extension field is key:value; value may be empty
        # If value contains tabs or spaces, keep as-is; ctags parsers allow it
        parts.append(f"{k}:{v}")
    return "\t" + "\t".join(parts)


def make_tagname_variants(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> List[str]:
    variants = {base}
    if base.lower() != base:
        variants.add(base.lower())
    if base.upper() != base:
        variants.add(base.upper())
    # Mixed case variations
    if len(base) >= 3:
        variants.add(base[0].upper() + base[1:])
        variants.add(base[0].lower() + base[1:])
    # Ensure at least one duplicate exact name possible
    return list(variants)


def generate_entries(rng: random.Random, sorted_method: int) -> List[str]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    # Choose a few base names and create variants to exercise find/findNext
    bases = rng.sample(WORDS, k=min(5, len(WORDS)))
    for b in bases:
        variants = make_tagname_variants(rng, b)
        # Group name to tag duplicates
        group_id = b.lower()
        # For each variant, create one or more entries
        for name in variants:
            count = 1 + (1 if rng.random() < 0.4 else 0)  # sometimes duplicates
            for _ in range(count):
                file_path = rand_choice(rng, FILES)
                # Randomly choose exCmd style
                if rng.random() < 0.6:
                    ex = make_pattern_excmd(rng, name)
                else:
                    ex = make_line_excmd(rng)
                kind_letter, _ = rand_choice(rng, KINDS)
                fields = make_ext_fields(rng, kind_letter, group_id if rng.random() < 0.7 else "")
                line = f"{name}\t{file_path}\t{ex};\"" + assemble_ext_fields(fields)
                lines.append(line)
    # Optionally add a few entries missing some optional parts (e.g., no fields)
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        name = rand_choice(rng, WORDS)
        file_path = rand_choice(rng, FILES)
        ex = make_pattern_excmd(rng, name) if rng.random() < 0.5 else make_line_excmd(rng)
        line = f"{name}\t{file_path}\t{ex};\""
        lines.append(line)

    # Sorting according to method: 0 unsorted, 1 sorted (C, case-sensitive), 2 foldcase
    if sorted_method == 1:
        lines.sort(key=lambda s: s.split("\t", 1)[0])
    elif sorted_method == 2:
        lines.sort(key=lambda s: s.split("\t", 1)[0].lower())
    # else leave unsorted
    return lines


def generate_header(rng: random.Random, sorted_method: int, format_ver: int) -> List[str]:
    header = []
    # Always include at least FILE_FORMAT and FILE_SORTED for richer behavior
    header.append(f"!_TAG_FILE_FORMAT\t{format_ver}\t/extended format/")
    header.append(f"!_TAG_FILE_SORTED\t{sorted_method}\t/0=unsorted, 1=sorted, 2=foldcase/")
    # Optionally include others
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        header.append("!_TAG_PROGRAM_AUTHOR\tJane Doe\tjdoe@example.com")
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        header.append("!_TAG_PROGRAM_NAME\tutagsgen")
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        header.append("!_TAG_PROGRAM_URL\thttps://example.invalid/ctags")
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        header.append("!_TAG_PROGRAM_VERSION\t1.2.3")
    return header


def clamp_bytes(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(data) <= MAX_BYTES:
        return data
    # Keep header and as many lines as fit
    return data[:MAX_BYTES]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide sorted method and format
    format_ver = 2 if rng.random() < 0.85 else 1
    sorted_method = rng.choices([0, 1, 2], weights=[0.3, 0.5, 0.2])[0]

    header = generate_header(rng, sorted_method, format_ver)
    entries = generate_entries(rng, sorted_method)

    # Shuffle a bit even if sorted_method says sorted=0; for sorted methods, entries already sorted
    if sorted_method == 0:
        rng.shuffle(entries)

    all_lines = header + entries

    # Ensure presence of at least one easily searchable common name with multiple matches
    # Name: FindMe
    extras: List[str] = []
    if not any(l.split("\t", 1)[0].lower() == "findme" for l in entries):
        for i in range(2):
            ex = make_pattern_excmd(rng, "FindMe") if i == 0 else make_line_excmd(rng)
            ext = assemble_ext_fields(make_ext_fields(rng, "f", "findme"))
            extras.append(f"FindMe\tsrc/main.c\t{ex};\"{ext}")
    all_lines.extend(extras)

    # Join lines with newlines; tags files are text files
    content = ("\n".join(all_lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8", errors="strict")

    return clamp_bytes(content)
